title: How much should an “independent” AI 3D benchmark disclose about brand relationships?
author: chiron-cooks
selftext:
I’ve been looking at AI 3D tools for game-dev stuff lately, mainly trying to get a better sense of how tools like Tripo and Meshy compare for generating assets.

While watching Stefan’s Tripo vs Meshy comparison, I noticed Top3D Arena being used/referenced, so I ended up checking Top3D too.

What caught my attention was how strongly it positions itself as “The independent benchmark for 3D AI Generators” with “No paid placement, no brand bias.”

At first I didn’t think much of it, but then I noticed Stefan / Stefan 3D AI Lab was also listed as a judge for an official Tripo rendering competition.

Then there’s also a Tripo Studio link tied specifically to Stefan using \`via=stefan\` and an \`invite\_code\`.

That combination made me stop for a sec. Not because it proves anything shady, but because when I’m comparing tools for an actual game-dev workflow, an “independent” benchmark carries a lot more weight than a normal creator review.

I have no idea if the referral-style link involves credits, rewards, commission, or just tracking, and being a competition judge obviously doesn’t mean rankings were influenced.

But would you expect relationships like these to be disclosed somewhere directly on the benchmark/review pages?

For people here using AI 3D tools for game assets, how much transparency do you expect from comparison sites before you trust their rankings between tools like Tripo, Meshy, etc.?

comments.author: IcyBother8850
comments.body: I just bought Meshy coz its on a huge sale now, for building my 3D isometric survival RPG I don't even use/need the highest quality options. I assume the same can be said for 90% of devs. So comparison videos unless you are trying to push some cutting edge graphics game are kinda pointless tbh.
